elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 4.2(a) still requires the Company (Customer) to pay HDI a "Termination Payment" equal to three months of Section 3.1 fees, and 4.2(c) retains the eight-instalment payment mechanic, so a Customer-payable liquidated amount survives.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: 4.2(a) as rendered: "the Company shall pay to HDI an early-termination fee (the 'Termination Payment')" — the former Net-Sales-based stipulated sum is gone and the only Customer-payable liquidated amount is now expressly characterised as an early-termination fee triggered by Company termination.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: "in an amount equal to the fees payable under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date" — the amount is fixed at (and therefore cannot exceed) three months of the Section 3.1 fees, replacing the uncapped 50%-of-excess-Net-Sales formula.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: "which shall be the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement" — express exclusivity statement covering the whole Agreement, not just Section 4.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the recast 4.2(a) converts the Net-Sales-based stipulated sum into an early-termination fee, fixes it at three months of Section 3.1 fees (within the three-month threshold, not exceeding it), and declares it the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company.
Preferred level is correctly not claimed: a Customer-payable liquidated amount and its instalment mechanic remain, so 'no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer' is not achieved.

Minimality holds: only the operative formula sentence in 4.2(a) was rewritten; the exclusivity phrase is required by the third fallback element; favourable retained provisions 4.2(b) (no payment where the amount is zero or less; no HDI payment obligation) and 4.2(c) (eight quarterly instalments) are untouched, and no survival tail, expense language, or extra procedure was added.

Intent is preserved: the termination trigger (Company termination, including via the Section 4.1 ninety-day notice), the defined terms "Termination Payment" and "Termination Date", the Section 3.1 fee reference, and the quarterly payment timing all remain coherent with no dangling cross-reference or contradictory sentence.

Drafting note only (not a defect): retained 4.2(b)'s zero-or-negative test is now largely vestigial because a three-months-of-fees amount cannot be negative; it is inoperative rather than contradictory, and deleting it would itself risk a minimality failure, but the drafter may wish to confirm the parties accept it as surplusage.
